html:
The Atakapa-Ishak were an Indigenous people of the Gulf Coast of southwestern Louisiana and southeastern Texas, around the lower Sabine, Calcasieu and Vermilion rivers. Ishak, "the people", was their own name; Atakapa came from a Choctaw word meaning "man eater".

They lived by fishing, gathering shellfish and hunting in the marshes and prairies, and their language is an isolate. Related bands included the Akokisa near Galveston Bay. Neighbours were the Chitimacha to the east, the Bidai inland and the Karankawa along the Texas coast.

French and Spanish traders reached them in the 1700s, and epidemics and the cattle ranches of Louisiana reduced them sharply. By the 1800s survivors had merged with Creole and other communities. Descendants have revived the name in recent decades. See also Atakapa.
